headline: Public repos and partial audit evidence confirmed; on-chain Solana program verification and audit PDF contents not directly fetched this run
short_headline: Partial audit coverage, Solana verify unconfirmed

findings.text: Sanctum's programs run on Solana, which uses a different verification model than EVM. The S repo includes a '.verified-build.json' file and lists mainnet program hashes for S Controller and pricing programs, indicating use of solana-verify tooling. However, Solana Explorer / SolanaFM verification status could not be directly confirmed via a fetch this run. The DeFiPunkd API does not support Solana (chainId not listed). On-chain verification status recorded as unknown for this run.

Public source repos exist at github.com/igneous-labs (97 repos). Key repos include 'S' (the INF/Infinity multi-LST program) and 'sanctum-unstake-program'. The unstake program README explicitly pins mainnet deploy at commit 11aac05b22794e6c2c3366dbb7141f4c61845c24. The S repo lists mainnet program hashes (e.g., S Controller hash 9bbcaada...) in its README. Both repos contain 'audits/' directories confirming audit files are present, though subdirectory contents could not be fetched this run.

Sanctum's blog (learn.sanctum.so/blog/solana-liquid-staking-guide) states Infinity has three audits from OtterSec, Sec3, and Neodyme, and that the SPL stake pool program (which underlies validator LSTs) has nine independent audits. The staking-as-a-service page references 'audited programs'. The S and sanctum-unstake-program repos each contain 'audits/' folders. However, audit PDFs/reports were not directly fetched, so specific commit scopes and dates could not be recorded. Audit coverage specific to the validator LST programs (as distinct from the Infinity pool) was not independently confirmed.

Named auditors include OtterSec, Sec3 (formerly Soteria/a Solana-focused security firm), and Neodyme — all recognized Solana ecosystem security firms. None are on the EVM-focused recognized-firm list in the rubric (Trail of Bits, Zellic, OpenZeppelin, etc.), though OtterSec and Neodyme are broadly recognized for Solana program audits. This introduces orange-at-best ambiguity per the rubric's 'unknown firm' clause, though the firms are not unknown in the Solana context.

The S repo README states 'Development of the INF program is now at https://github.com/igneous-labs/inf-1.5', indicating the codebase has migrated since the audited version. The S repo has 905 commits on master. Whether post-migration changes have been re-audited could not be confirmed without fetching the audit directory contents or the inf-1.5 repo. This represents potential post-audit drift risk for the Infinity component, which is a fund-custody program.

Solana programs use BPF/SBF loader upgrade authority rather than EVM proxy patterns. The S repo's '.verified-build.json' and listed program hashes indicate the team tracks deployments. No proxy/implementation split applies; the relevant verification question is whether the deployed .so bytecode matches the published source. This was not confirmed via a Solana explorer fetch this run.

steelman.red: No audit PDF was directly fetched and verified this run, no on-chain program verification was confirmed via Solana Explorer, and the codebase has migrated from the audited 'S' repo to 'inf-1.5' with unknown re-audit coverage — a fund-custody program with unconfirmed current-version audit is effectively unverified.
steelman.orange: Public source repos exist with audit directories and mainnet commit pins, recognized Solana audit firms (OtterSec, Neodyme) are cited by Sanctum's own docs for Infinity (3 audits) and SPL stake pool (9 audits), and the team maintains verifiable-build infrastructure; however, audit PDF contents were not fetched, Solana on-chain verification was not confirmed, and post-migration (S → inf-1.5) re-audit status is unknown.
steelman.green: Three audits from recognized Solana firms cover Infinity, nine audits cover the SPL stake pool base used by validator LSTs, public repos with commit-pinned mainnet deploys exist, and verifiable-build tooling (.verified-build.json) is in use — together this represents a strong verifiability posture for a Solana liquid staking protocol.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because: while public repos and cited audits from recognized Solana firms exist (V3/V4), audit PDF contents were not fetched in this run to confirm commit scope and recency, on-chain bytecode verification on Solana Explorer could not be confirmed (V1), the active codebase has migrated to inf-1.5 with unknown re-audit coverage (V5 drift), and the named auditors (OtterSec, Sec3, Neodyme) fall outside the EVM-specific recognized-firm list in the rubric. The green steel-man is weakened by the unconfirmed post-migration audit and inability to fetch on-chain verification; the red steel-man is weakened by clear evidence of a public repo, audit directories, and cited third-party reviews from known Solana security firms.

evidence.shows: Sanctum website confirms GitHub org at github.com/igneous-labs, product structure (Infinity pool, validator LSTs, staking-as-a-service), docs at learn.sanctum.so/docs, governance forum at research.sanctum.so, CLOUD token
Igneous Labs GitHub org: 97 public repositories, 'building the Sanctum protocol'. Key repos visible: S (INF multi-LST AMM), sanctum-unstake-program, sanctum-lst-list, sanctum-spl-stake-pool-sdk

S repo (INF program): contains audits/ folder, .verified-build.json, README lists mainnet program hashes for S Controller (9bbcaada...), Flat Fee Pricing (b09e282d...), and multiple SOL value calculators. Notes development moved to inf-1.5. 905 commits on master. Verifiable build instructions included.
Unstake program repo: contains audits/ folder, README pins mainnet deploy at commit 11aac05b22794e6c2c3366dbb7141f4c61845c24
Sanctum blog states Infinity has three audits (OtterSec, Sec3, Neodyme) and SPL stake pool program has nine independent audits securing billions of dollars. Validator LSTs use SPL stake pool program.
Staking-as-a-service page states service is 'Built on audited programs, custom-support SLAs, and flawless uptime'

Third-party assessment notes: Infinity has three audits, multisig has at least 4 signers, no timelock exists, governance by 11-member multisig including Jito/Jupiter/Laine. Protocol version launched 2024.

unknowns: V1: Solana on-chain program verification status (via Solana Explorer or SolanaFM) could not be confirmed — DeFiPunkd API does not support Solana chainId and Solana explorer fetch was not attempted in this run due to fetch budget constraints
V3: Audit PDF/report contents for the S repo audits/ and sanctum-unstake-program audits/ folders not fetched this run — specific commit hashes in scope, audit dates, and exact findings unknown
V3: Audit coverage for validator LST programs specifically (as distinct from Infinity/INF pool and SPL stake pool base) not confirmed from fetched sources
V5: Re-audit coverage for inf-1.5 (migration destination from S repo) unknown — whether the post-migration codebase has been audited by a recognized firm was not confirmed
V2: No commit SHA was pinned for the S/INF repo mainnet deploy from fetched sources (program hashes listed but not mapped to a git SHA)
V1-offchain: Solana Explorer / SolanaFM fetch for deployed program verification not attempted — no Solana block explorer was fetched in this run

protocol_metadata.about: Sanctum (built by Igneous Labs) is Solana's leading liquid staking infrastructure, enabling users to stake SOL with specific validators and receive tradeable liquid staking tokens (LSTs) in return. Validators or protocols can launch their own branded LST (e.g., laineSOL, JupSOL, bbSOL) via Sanctum's Staking-as-a-Service offering, which manages stake accounts and delegation on their behalf. Sanctum also operates the Infinity pool, a multi-LST AMM that provides unified liquidity across all supported LSTs, allowing instant swaps between any two LSTs using stake account-based pricing without external oracles. The underlying programs build on Solana's audited SPL stake pool program, with Infinity itself receiving three independent audits from OtterSec, Sec3, and Neodyme.
